benchmark.name: Mumford ECHR citation context v1
benchmark.import_note: Re-imported from the same verified archive on 2026-10-28. The imported files hash differently from the 2026-08-21 import (def75b3b…, 7a0ef6db…); document, curated-annotation and selected-annotation counts are unchanged.

software.name: echr-py
software.source_snapshot_note: The benchmark was evaluated directly from two clean detached worktrees at this commit on branch fix/citation-occurrence-repairs; the per-file hashes independently identify the code used.

selection.selection_schema: sorted item IDs, one per line
selection.input_note: HUDOC search returned Cloudflare 403 throughout the refresh, and the 2026-08-21 lookup cache no longer exists. Source metadata, the English HUDOC catalogue and source/target HTML were therefore read offline from a local HUDOC snapshot. The sorted selection hash equals the 2026-08-21 selection; the catalogue is English-only, so French-only targets cannot resolve and SCL and document coverage are lower than in the August run for reasons of input, not code.

same_input_baseline.alignment_change_note: One-to-one alignment is unchanged from 0.2.5 (5,315). The intermediate repair commit lost one alignment in Smirnova and Smirnova v. Russia (001-241461), where the printed name was split into two occurrences; this commit keeps the repeated applicant name in one locus and recovers it.

previous_audit.comparability_note: Different inputs (online lookup cache and catalogue). The August run recorded no separate-opinion or appendix occurrences; this run records 1,407 and 129, which fall outside the XMI reference text and are abstained in projection. Not a like-for-like comparison.

commands: echr-py citations resolve --in CASES --catalog CATALOG --out RESOLVED --offline
echr-py citations locate --in CASES --resolution-dir RESOLVED --catalog CATALOG --out OCCURRENCES --html-dir SOURCE_HTML --target-html-dir TARGET_HTML --scope inclusive --offline --resolve-paragraphs
qualifications: Mumford annotations are selective and do not supply exhaustive negatives, so this result does not estimate detector precision.
The reference supplies no canonical target item IDs or structured target-paragraph links; document and paragraph figures are coverage, not accuracy.
SCL resolution and exact-document identification rates are automatic coverage; this benchmark does not independently verify every promoted procedural document.
Application-number agreement is conditional on an automatic identification and does not establish exact procedural-document accuracy.
The comparator requires the annotation's bibliographic identity in addition to span overlap; another authority inside a broad annotation span is not a match.
The frozen XMI source supplies THE LAW majority text only. Opinions, footnotes, and other document sections are outside this comparison rather than false negatives.
No third-party source archive, raw annotation row, HUDOC source document, lookup cache, or raw benchmark output is bundled with echr-py.
Inputs were read offline from a local HUDOC snapshot; three cited target documents had no HTML in it, and paragraph-unavailable rows otherwise reflect non-paragraph or unmappable targets.
The offline catalogue is English-only, so French-only targets remain unresolved; SCL and exact-document coverage are lower than the August 2026 run for that reason.
